si.t: How to use the scoring spreadsheet

A car's score is calculated on the right hand side of the spreadsheet. 3 points for a first place finish, 2 points for a 2nd place finish, and 1 point for a 3rd place finish. This always causes confusion so you may want to explain this before the race.
After all heats have been run, the car with the highest score wins. Manually enter the overall finish for each car at the bottom of the scoring columns, and determine if any runoffs are necessary.
Be sure to save this file at the end of the race.
Notes and tips for having a successful derby
As a minimum, have the following people to run the race
2) A car handler to get the cars from the pit area and hand them to the starter,
3) A finish judge to determine the finish place for each lane, and to tell the finish order to the scorer,
4) A scorer to run this spreadsheet,
5) and a runner to carry cars from the finish line back to the pit area.
During check-in, have someone write down names and car numbers on a sheet of paper while you type the names and car numbers into this spreedsheet.
After all racers have been entered, select the appropriate scoring sheet for the number of cars.
After selecting the approprate sheet for the number of cars to run, select "Full Screen" mode from the "View" menu. Also select a zoom percentage to show the sheet as large as possible.
You may need to resize the bottom row of the scoring sheet to not clip off the bottom of the cub names
You can change the scoring sheet title by editing cell C50 on the "Names" sheet
The race order is based on the Partial Perfect-N (PPN) Charts
A PPN chart is one which satisfies these conditions:
2. Equality of opposition is optimized, i.e., no head to head matchup count exceeds another by more than 1.
1. Each car races the same number of times in each lane (which implies that the number 'of races is a multiple of the number of cars)
During the race, select the current heat by entering the heat number in cell H2. The current heat names and car numbers show up at the top.
When a heat has been run, enter the lane number for the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd finishes
If you are projecting the results onto a screen, pause for a bit to allow racers to see the finish results for that heat. Then go back up to cell H2 and change to the next heat number.

Work sheets are locked to prevent accidental changes to cells that aren't normally edited during a race. Cells that you type in are a pale yellow color. Unlock the sheet to allow editing of cell formulas and formats
The car lane assignments follow the Partial Perfect N algorithm but you can easily change these assignments. Unhide columns B, C, D, and E to see lane assignments.
Be sure to assign each car in the pack (not just the den) a unique number so there is never any confusion about cars.

In these column on the row for each heat are the lane assignments. A 1 means the first car from the Names sheet, 2 is the second car, etc. The cell formulas will work with any car lane assignments without changes.
Developed by Bob Baggerman, bob@scoutdb.org (17 Jan 2005)

This scoring spreadsheet can handle from 3 to 15 racers. Cub scout names and car numbers are entered in the "Names" sheet before the race. Start entering names and car numbers on line 2 and don't skip any lines. Put the den title or other title in C1.
